summary: In this Christmas special episode of the Lord of Spirits, hosts Fr. Andrew Stephen Damick and Fr. Stephen De Young explore the surprising presence of astrology in the Bible and ancient Jewish tradition. They begin by discussing the discovery of zodiac mosaics in Galilean synagogues, which prompts an investigation into how ancient Israelites understood the stars and their connection to angelic beings. The hosts distinguish biblical astrology from pagan astrology and modern horoscopes, emphasizing that heavenly bodies are not independent gods but servants of the one true God, communicating His message through their movements. They delve into Psalm 19, interpreting the 'line' of the sun as the ecliptic, and show how St. Paul in Romans 10 uses this psalm to argue that the gospel has been proclaimed through the heavens. The episode also explores the association of the twelve tribes of Israel with zodiac signs, the song of Deborah in Judges 5, and the role of the Magi in recognizing the birth of Christ through a celestial sign. The hosts address listener questions about the influence of stars on personality, the 'gospel in the stars' theory, and the recent Jupiter-Saturn conjunction, ultimately concluding that the star of Bethlehem was a unique celestial event that announced the incarnation of Christ, hidden from the demonic powers until its revelation. The episode closes with reflections on the restoration of humanity's connection to creation through Christ.

entities.title: Philo of Alexandria
entities.summary: A Hellenistic Jewish philosopher who discussed the Jewish view of the sun, moon, and stars as lesser officials in God's divine government, contrasting it with pagan worship of these bodies.

entities.title: St. Ignatius of Antioch
entities.summary: An early church father and martyr whose epistle to the Ephesians describes the star that announced Christ's birth, causing confusion among the stars (angels) and leading to the destruction of the ancient kingdom of demons.

entities.title: St. Paul
entities.summary: The Apostle Paul, who in Romans 10 quotes Psalm 19 to argue that the gospel has been proclaimed through the heavens, and in 1 Corinthians 2 speaks of the hidden wisdom of God unknown to the rulers of this age.

entities.title: Herod the Great
entities.summary: The king of Judea at the time of Christ's birth, who ordered the massacre of infants in an attempt to kill the newborn king. His death is used as a benchmark for dating Jesus' birth.

entities.title: Magi
entities.summary: Wise men from the East, likely Persian astrologers, who saw a celestial sign announcing the birth of a king of the Jews and traveled to worship him. They are associated with the star of Bethlehem.

entities.title: Zodiac
entities.summary: The twelve constellations along the ecliptic, which in ancient Jewish tradition were associated with the twelve tribes of Israel and depicted in synagogue mosaics.

concepts.title: Biblical Astrology
concepts.summary: The understanding that the sun, moon, and stars are associated with angelic beings and serve as messengers of God, communicating knowledge and proclaiming the gospel through their movements. This is distinct from pagan astrology and modern horoscopes.

concepts.title: Ecliptic
concepts.summary: The path the sun follows over the course of a year, referred to as the 'line' in Psalm 19:4. It is the region of the sky where the zodiac constellations are found, and its significance is tied to the sun's movement and the communication of knowledge.

concepts.title: Divine Council
concepts.summary: The heavenly assembly of angelic beings who serve God and participate in His governance of creation. The concept is used to explain the hierarchy of spiritual beings and the mystery of God's plans hidden from angels until revealed.

concepts.title: Messianic Secret
concepts.summary: The idea that Christ's identity and mission were hidden from the demonic powers until the appropriate time, as described by St. Ignatius of Antioch and St. Paul. This secrecy was part of God's plan to defeat death and the devil.

concepts.title: Theosis
concepts.summary: The process of becoming like God, often described as deification. In this episode, it is connected to the promise to Abraham that his descendants would be like the stars, and to the idea that humans are destined to join the divine council.

claims.text: The sun, moon, and stars are associated with angelic beings who serve as messengers and agents of God, not independent deities.
The gospel is proclaimed through the movements of the heavens, as St. Paul argues in Romans 10, quoting Psalm 19.
The twelve tribes of Israel are associated with the twelve zodiac signs, as seen in the breastplate of the high priest and the blessings of Jacob.

The star of Bethlehem was not the recent Jupiter-Saturn conjunction but a unique celestial event that occurred on September 11, 3 BC, which was also the Jewish New Year and a day associated with kingship.
The date of Christmas, December 25, is not derived from pagan festivals but from the calculation of the Annunciation on March 25, based on the tradition of integral age.

scriptural_links.summary: Describes the heavens declaring the glory of God and the sun's path (ecliptic) as a means of communication. Quoted by St. Paul in Romans 10 to show that the gospel has been heard by all.
St. Paul quotes Psalm 19 to argue that the gospel has been proclaimed through the heavens, implying that the movements of the stars communicate the message of Christ.

The song of Deborah describes the stars fighting from their courses against Sisera, and the faithful being like the sun in strength, illustrating the involvement of heavenly beings in earthly battles.

Describes a sign in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, standing on the moon, and a dragon. Some interpret this as an astronomical event, but the hosts argue it is not a direct reference to the star of Bethlehem.
Mentions the morning stars singing together and the sons of God shouting for joy at creation, linking stars with angels and their worship.

glossary.definition: The apparent path of the sun across the sky over the course of a year, which is the basis for the zodiac.
A Hebrew word for constellations, used in Job 38:32, referring to the twelve signs of the zodiac.
A tradition that a prophet's death occurs on the same date as his conception, used to calculate the date of the Annunciation and thus Christmas.
A title for the Virgin Mary meaning 'God-bearer,' emphasizing that she gave birth to God incarnate.
The heavenly assembly of angels and other spiritual beings who serve God and participate in His governance.
